feedback:
Decision: approve. This candidate changes one field from the best raced design (iteration 6, score 85.60, reproduced exactly in iteration 9): base_speed 1.0 to 0.9. Geometry, kp 4.0, ki 0.05, kd 0.30, sensor weights (±0.05 m, 16 mm) and line_loss search_left are unchanged.

Why the test is sound: oval progress rose 0.137 (speed 1.4, iteration 4), 0.318 (speed 1.2, iteration 5), then 0.3425 (speed 1.0, iteration 6). The gain is flattening, so the next step down is the untested lever for oval max_error, which has stayed at 0.0605 to 0.0626 across iterations 3 to 6, just over the 0.06 m limit. Iteration 8 showed that changing sensing span can hurt sharply, and iteration 7 showed that lowering kd cut oval progress, so neither is the next change. s-bend and slalom have shown one line-loss event per run under every recovery direction and speed tried (iterations 0 to 6), so speed is not their limit and I do not expect this race to change them.

What I do not know: whether 0.9 is too slow to hold oval progress. Do not treat this candidate as better than iteration 6 until the race shows it. Iteration 6 stays the fallback, and it can be re-approved in the next iteration.

How to read the race: (a) If oval progress stays at or above about 0.33 and oval max_error falls below 0.06 with 0 oval line losses, keep base_speed 0.9 as the new best. (b) If oval progress falls well below 0.3425 while max_error stays near 0.06, speed 0.9 is too slow; re-approve iteration 6 (base_speed 1.0) and stop lowering speed. (c) If the oval holds but max_error is still at or above 0.06 with steering_oscillation above 0.15, the next lever is kd 0.25, changed alone. Because this is iteration 10 of 12, with one iteration left after it, use the next review to decide between the best of 0.9 and 1.0 and approve that one.
requested_changes: If oval progress holds at or above about 0.33 at base_speed 0.9 with oval max_error below 0.06, keep 0.9 as the best design and approve it again next iteration. Evidence: speed 1.0 gave progress 0.3425 and speed 1.2 gave 0.318, so the trend is flattening, not reversing.

If oval progress falls well below 0.3425 at base_speed 0.9, return base_speed to 1.0 with every other field unchanged and re-approve iteration 6 (score 85.60, reproduced in iteration 9). Evidence: iteration 6 is the best raced result and its repeat was identical.

Do not change the sensor layout again. Iteration 8 (spread ±0.08 m) cut oval progress to 0.2039 and collapsed s-bend and slalom, while s-bend and slalom have shown one line loss per run under every recovery direction and speed tried.
